DELIVERABLE: Rebuild the image every 8 hours from a CI cron job that clones main, installs dependencies, warms caches and publishes a tagged image; new sessions start from the newest successful tag and sync the repo before writing.
BOUNDARY: A rebuild schedule alone is not enough: export the age of the newest good image as a metric, compare it with the 24h staleness target, and page on-call when the age exceeds the target or any build fails.
EVIDENCE: Metric graph of image age staying under 24h, a deliberately failed build that triggered the alert, and session logs showing the image tag used.

DELIVERABLE: Cron a build every 6 hours (four runs per day, safely inside 24h), publish with a timestamp tag, and have the API pick the latest valid image.
BOUNDARY: Watch image freshness continuously: a gauge for time since the last successful build, and a notification to the owning team when it passes 24 hours or when a build job fails; sessions still fetch main before any write.
EVIDENCE: Alert rule definitions, a dry-run where the build was broken on purpose and the notification arrived, and a dashboard of image age percentiles.

DELIVERABLE: Rebuild the image every 8 hours from a CI cron job that clones main, installs dependencies, warms caches and publishes a tagged image; the schedule is derived from the 24h staleness budget.
BOUNDARY: Sessions start from the newest tag and sync the repo before writing; on-call is alerted whenever a build job fails.
EVIDENCE: Build logs per run and session records of which tag was used.

DELIVERABLE: Rebuild every 8 hours from CI, sized so two missed runs still fit inside the 24h limit, and publish tagged images that sessions pick up automatically.
BOUNDARY: A dashboard plots image age against the 24h target and lists failed builds; nobody is sent anything, people look when they need to. Sessions sync before writing.
EVIDENCE: Dashboard screenshots and build logs.

DELIVERABLE: Automate an image build every 24 hours, publish it as the current tag, and recycle pool sandboxes so each is replaced by one from the new image once it is ready.
BOUNDARY: Measure the age of the image in each pool entry and of the newest build against the 72h patch target, and alert the platform channel when the age nears or exceeds the target or the nightly build fails; the cadence alone would not reveal a silently broken pipeline.
EVIDENCE: Per-pool image age metric, an alert test with a forced build failure, and a count of sessions served from images older than 72h (should be zero).

DELIVERABLE: Nightly scheduled build (well under 72h), warm entries expire and are recreated when a new build completes, and sessions start from the latest valid image.
BOUNDARY: Track how old the serving image is against the 72 hour target on a metric, and send a page to on-call when that threshold is breached or a scheduled build errors out.
EVIDENCE: Metric history, the alert firing in a drill, and pool logs of entry recreation times.

DELIVERABLE: Build automatically every 24 hours and recycle warm pool entries when a new image lands, so patches reach sandboxes in at most about a day.
BOUNDARY: Alert the on-call engineer if the nightly build fails; sessions still sync the repo before writes.
EVIDENCE: Build logs and pool turnover logs.

DELIVERABLE: Build every 24 hours, expire warm sandboxes as each build completes, and start sessions from the latest image.
BOUNDARY: The age of the serving image is tracked on a dashboard against the 72h target and failed builds appear in the CI log; no automatic messages go out.
EVIDENCE: Dashboard history and CI logs.

DELIVERABLE: Rebuild more often than weekly, for example every 3 days, since a Sunday-only build reaches the 7-day limit exactly at the next build; publish each image with its build timestamp and clone commit.
BOUNDARY: Add monitoring of image age against the 7-day compliance target, and alert owners when the age passes a threshold such as 5 days or when any build fails, since a failed Sunday build otherwise leaves the old image serving past the limit.
EVIDENCE: Age metric for the current image, alert history including a forced failure drill, and the build timestamps recorded on each image.

DELIVERABLE: Schedule a build every 72 hours with a 40-minute timeout, tag by timestamp, and have sessions use the newest valid image plus a repo sync.
BOUNDARY: Emit the age of the live image as a metric, compare it with the 7 day ceiling, and notify the team on breach or on a failed build.
EVIDENCE: Dashboard of image age, a notification test on a broken build, and tag timestamps.

DELIVERABLE: Rebuild every 3 days instead of weekly, leaving slack for a failed run, and publish images with timestamp and clone commit tags.
BOUNDARY: Sessions use the newest valid image and sync before writing; the build job retries once on failure and pages the owner if the retry fails.
EVIDENCE: Build history and retry counts.

DELIVERABLE: Rebuild every 3 days with the build timestamp stamped on the image, so one missed run still fits within 7 days.
BOUNDARY: A dashboard shows image age versus the 7-day limit, and failed builds show red in CI; it is reviewed in the weekly ops sync with no automatic messaging.
EVIDENCE: Dashboard history and CI statuses.

DELIVERABLE: Return only when the fix removes duplicates on 30 replayed nights in staging and a reproduction script fails before the fix and passes after.
BOUNDARY: Before returning, a fresh verifier instance that did not build the fix runs an adversarial audit against the listed failure modes (late-arriving data, retries, idempotency keys, timezone cutoffs); the worker cannot return while a blocking finding with evidence is open.
EVIDENCE: Reproduction output, replay results, and the verifier's findings log with each blocking item closed by a rerun.

DELIVERABLE: The run returns only after the candidate fix survives an audit performed by a separate auditor agent started in a clean context with just the repo diff, the checklist and the staging access.
BOUNDARY: Findings count as blocking only if backed by a failing replay or counterexample; blocking findings go back to the worker with a retry cap, and the worker is not allowed to declare itself done.
EVIDENCE: Replay logs, the auditor's report, and the commit hash audited.

DELIVERABLE: Return only when the fix removes duplicates on 30 replayed nights and a reproduction fails before the fix and passes after.
BOUNDARY: As the last step the same agent runs an adversarial self-audit against the failure-mode list (retries, idempotency keys, late data, timezones) and fixes anything it finds before returning; it cannot return while a finding is open.
EVIDENCE: Replay output and the self-audit notes.

DELIVERABLE: A fresh verifier instance audits the candidate fix against the failure-mode checklist and writes a report.
BOUNDARY: The report is advisory: the worker returns as soon as it is confident the fix holds, and may skip findings it disagrees with.
EVIDENCE: Replay results and the verifier report.

DELIVERABLE: Final audit runs on a fresh independent auditor instance, not the orchestrator, against the enumerated failure modes (wire compatibility, deadline propagation, auth metadata, streaming backpressure); the migration is returned only after it passes.
BOUNDARY: The auditor gets the repository diff, test commands and the checklist only, without the orchestrator's transcript, notes or rationale, so it cannot inherit the builders' assumptions; the extra tokens are accepted.
EVIDENCE: Auditor report with reproduced failures, test output tied to the audited commit, and the list of non-blocking findings.

DELIVERABLE: An independent verifier started in a clean context performs the end-of-run adversarial audit; neither the orchestrator nor any worker may audit its own output, and the return waits on its verdict.
BOUNDARY: Give it just the final artifact (diff, running service in staging) and the checklist; withhold the orchestrator's summaries, reasoning and history. Only findings with a failing check or counterexample block.
EVIDENCE: Verifier's reproduction commands and outputs, the audited commit hash, and the retry log for blocking findings.

DELIVERABLE: The orchestrator runs the final adversarial audit using the failure-mode checklist, since it holds all the context, and returns only when the audit passes.
BOUNDARY: It audits the candidate against wire compatibility, deadlines, auth metadata and backpressure; blocking findings need evidence.
EVIDENCE: Audit notes and test output.

DELIVERABLE: A separate auditor agent in a fresh context runs the final audit, and the migration returns only when it passes.
BOUNDARY: The auditor receives the orchestrator's full transcript, its working notes and its summary of what was verified, so it can start fast; blocking findings need evidence.
EVIDENCE: Auditor report and test output.
